headline: Nike Wants to Triple Its India Business in Five Years

image.licence: Nike official press image (newsroom, 21 Oct 2026), editorial use, credited 'Image: Nike'
image.author: Nike
image.subject: Aerial of Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, with a Nike Swoosh mowed into the outfield; Marine Drive and the sea behind. Nike's own image for its Mumbai Indians kit deal. No people visible. The Mumbai Indians + Nike logo overlay over the sea is cropped out.

framing.note: bottom-anchored 1.15x crop removes the logo overlay (source y ~2300-2600); stadium at ~y 320-900 of 1350, Swoosh at ~y 575; headline over dark buildings; downscaled, no upscale

fact_sources.fact: Nike wants to triple its India business in the next five years (on stage at Investor Day, 17 Nov US time; not in the press release); COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy to CNBC
Sportico reported the India target as tripling sales over the next four years
First Nike investor day since 2017 (nine years)
Running, training, sportswear and cricket lead Nike's India push
Nike says it will have 'a complete cricket footwear line' when cricket returns to the Olympics in 2028
Cricket returns to the Olympics at LA 2028 for the first time in more than 100 years
Nike already sells cricket shoes in India, e.g. the Domain 3 (launched 13 Feb 2026; Domain 3 Low on nike.in)
Nike Vegam Run, Nike's first running shoe built for India, on sale since 1 Nov at ₹3,795 on Flipkart and select stores
Context: Nike is kit partner for Mumbai Indians' men's and women's teams from the 2027 season (announced 21 Oct 2026)
Lead tie-in: Complex 17 Nov 'Nike Investor Day 2026: Everything We Learned' (context only)
